about: The long run. Batch B-4471 of Maple Farm milk powder 800 g, 2,400 tins, 40 parties over 10 simulated days: 5 on the shipment records, 21 accounts found in the distributors' order systems (20 stores and Summit Foods, which runs its own copy of the agent), and 14 stores named by forwarders, Corner Mart among them. 36 are simulated parties with behaviour profiles; Harbour Market and Corner Mart answer real phones in the demo. Every store's tins are on the shelf when it hears of the recall and held four to twelve simulated hours later. Ends with only the slice's tins open (15 disputed, 25 still on the shelf at Corner Mart), so the recall cannot close.

recall.hazard: The lid seal may be faulty, so the powder can spoil. Do not use it; bring it back for a refund.

lid did not seal, the powder was hard and lumpy inside
lid was lifted, powder clumped and smelled sour

initial.say: We've got sixty on the shelf.
Sorry, I was reading the wrong line. The till says ten sold, and we pulled the other thirty into the back room. The batch code reads B-4471, and the till refused the sale.
The till says fifty sold. Thirty are pulled and held in the back, and forty went to Corner Mart. The batch code reads B-4471, and the till refused the sale.

dispute_followup.say: Checked the delivery notes. Twenty-five went to Corner Mart. The other fifteen are still in our back room, held.

initial.say: Twenty sold, per the till's sales report. The other sixty are pulled and held for return. The batch code reads B-4471, and the till refused the sale.
We received twenty-five, all still on the shelf. The batch code reads B-4471, and the till still sells it.

dispute_followup.say: No, twenty-five. I have the delivery note.
